title: ci-cd-rollback-breadcrumbs-canary-failure-2024-11-02
content:
Summary:
- Short: Canary rollout of inference-service v2.4.0-canary caused 5% canary to show large latency spikes and periodic 502/500 errors; rolled back to v2.3.1 at 2024-11-02T14:40Z.
- This doc is my breadcrumbs (commands run, logs, quick hypotheses) — notes for the postmortem and follow-ups.

Timeline (local times UTC):
- 14:05 — Started gradual canary (5%) via helm chart update -> image: redwood/inference:2.4.0-canary.
- 14:12 — Observed first latency spike on canary traces (p95 from 120ms -> 1.2s).
- 14:18 — Alerts: route inference-api-canary increased error rate; SLO violations shown in console.
- 14:25 — Scoped to canary pods: kubectl get pods -n inference | grep canary shows 3/3 pods READY then intermittent restarts on pod inference-canary-2.
- 14:40 — Rolled back canary to previous image (v2.3.1) and scaled down canary replicas. Error rate returned to baseline by 14:47.

Commands I ran (copy-paste-able):
- kubectl -n inference get svc,deploy,rs,po -l app=inference-service
- kubectl -n inference logs deployment/inference-canary --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl -n inference describe pod inference-canary-2
- kubectl -n inference exec -it inference-canary-2 -- /bin/bash -c 'top -b -n1 | head -n 20'
- kubectl -n inference exec -it inference-canary-2 -- curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:8080/health" -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n'
- kubectl -n inference port-forward svc/inference-canary 8080:8080 &
- curl -v http://localhost:8080/infer -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @sample_request.json
- helm history inference-service -n inference
- helm rollback inference-service 2 -n inference (rollback to v2.3.1 release)

Key log snippets (redacted):
- 2024-11-02T14:13:22Z ERROR [request-handler] request_id=abcd1234 status=502 backend_error=\"gRPC error: code=13 INTERNAL\" route=/v1/infer latency_ms=1250
- 2024-11-02T14:14:08Z WARN  [kv-cache] miss_count=342 prefix_cache_invalidate=true
- 2024-11-02T14:15:01Z ERROR [runtime] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
- goroutine 421 [running]:
- runtime.throw(0x12afc3b, 0x2a)
- ... (stack truncated)
- 2024-11-02T14:16:45Z ERROR [request-handler] request_id=efgh5678 status=500 err=\"out of memory\" alloc_bytes=153643392

Observed behavior / metrics:
- p50/p95/p99 on canary: 80ms / 1.2s / 3.8s (baseline v2.3.1: 75ms / 110ms / 220ms)
- CPU on canary pods spiked to ~95% for short bursts; memory RSS increased steadily vs baseline (avg +300MB).
- Pod restarts: 1 pod restarted 4x in 20 minutes.
- Prefetch/batching metrics: k/v cache miss rate jumped, leading to recomputation.

Immediate actions taken:
- Scaled canary down from 3 -> 1 to limit blast radius (kubectl scale deploy/inference-canary --replicas=1).
- Collected heap/profile from crashing pod (gcore + /proc/$pid/maps where possible). Saved to /tmp/canary-profiles/ (uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-debug/canary/2024-11-02/).
- Rolled back helm release to v2.3.1 (helm rollback inference-service 2 -n inference).
- Re-ran basic health checks and smoke tests on rollback.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Memory/regression in new runtime scheduling or batching code (highest likelihood) — small code change in PR 1872 modifies attention kernel selection and continuous batching thresholds. Correlates with increased memory and OOM errors.
2) New quantization flags enabled by default in 2.4.0-canary causing kernel incompatibility on our GPU images -> internal gRPC failures.
3) Configuration drift between cluster node types (canary pods scheduled on newer node family with different driver/kernel) — driver mismatch could cause sporadic gRPC errors and OOMs.
4) Third-party dependency bump (protobuf / grpc) leading to serialization or internal error paths.

Quick diffs / PRs to check:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1872 (changes: batching defaults, kernel selector)
- Commit: 7f2b1c3 changed default --quantize-runtime=true in chart values.yaml

Things to repro (next steps):
- Reproduce locally with same image tag: docker run --rm -it redwood/inference:2.4.0-canary bash -> run loadtest against local model with same batching config.
- Force canary pods scheduled onto same node class as stable (node selectors/affinity) to eliminate node family as cause.
- Start canary with QUANTIZE=false override (helm set image.tag=2.4.0-canary --set runtime.quantize=false) and observe memory/latency.
- Run pprof heap/cpu capture across lifecycle to see leaked allocations (capture right before crash).

Artifacts and versions observed:
- inference-service: 2.4.0-canary (image sha: sha256:aa11bb22cc33)
- inference-service-stable: 2.3.1 (sha256:dd44ee55ff66)
- helm chart: inference-service-chart v1.12.0 -> v1.13.0 (canary)
- model bundle: open-model-v1.0.3 (unchanged in this rollout)

Notes for postmortem / follow-up actions:
- Block next canary rollouts of 2.4.0-canary until we get a reproducible test or revert PR 1872.
- Add tighter resource limits/requests for canary releases to avoid OOM and surface misconfigs faster.
- Add canary-only profiling hooks that auto-trigger on p95 > 500ms for more deterministic captures.
- Run integration test that reproduces batching + cache pressure on CI (small cluster sim).
- Check node-driver versions for the nodes that scheduled canary pods: (kubectl get nodes -o wide) -> note: two canary pods landed on node gpu-nv24a-07 which is running driver 520.xx; stable pods were on gpu-nv24a-03 with driver 515.xx.

Related threads / tickets: 
- JIRA INF-3421 (investigate canary OOMs) — assigned to Ben Lee.
- Slack: #release-incidents thread (link above) has screenshots of Grafana and trace IDs.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Was the quantize=true flip intentional in PR 1872 or accidental? (ask PR author @Diego)
- Can we reliably reproduce with a single pod local run, or do we need to simulate multi-pod KV/cache pressure?
- If kernel selector change is the cause, can we add a guard to disable it when quantize=false?

Raw traces / anchors (IDs to paste into tracing UI):
- trace_id: 6f8b2d3a (high-latency sample at 14:12)
- trace_id: 9c1a4b54 (oom on inference-canary-2 at 14:15)

If anyone is picking this up: start with PR 1872 and the helm values diff, then try local run with quantize toggle. I uploaded builds and profiles to S3 bucket path above.

End of breadcrumbs.

Aisha
